A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ST-RCGP research. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching content despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations, financial-data experiments, temperature predictions, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds well-log fits, controlled weight-function analyses, outlier-timing tests, and temperature-coverage results.

M1.justification: The filtering updates, adaptive centering and shrinking functions, beta choice, and weighted hyperparameter objective are retained. The loss displayed in v2's main text was already derived in v1's appendix; the exponent sweep tests variants without changing the recommended method.

E1.justification: v2 adds well-log geological measurements containing sediment transitions and natural outliers (Appendix C.7, Figure 12). It also explicitly tests early versus late contamination. The original synthetic, financial, and temperature coverage remains.

E2.justification: The corresponding main comparisons retain STGP/GP, RCGP, relevance pursuit, and the MEP, MVI, and MLa methods. New appendix comparisons reuse existing comparators; newly cited outlier-rejection methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendices C.8–C.10 introduce an IMQ exponent sweep, controlled comparisons changing centering and shrinking while holding other parameters fixed, and early/late-outlier tests. Original splits, optimisation budgets, kernels, and reported temperature settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's beta/shrinking and optimisation-objective analyses, v2 tests exponent sensitivity, isolates adaptive centering and shrinking, examines outlier timing, and evaluates October temperature coverage (Figures 13–15 and 17). These substantially expand evidence about robustness mechanisms and calibration.

E5.justification: Mean/standard-deviation reporting and repeated-run counts remain unchanged, including five runtime repeats and 20 simulated crash realizations. Additional posterior bands and coverage curves extend uncertainty analyses already used in v1; no new significance tests or repeated-run estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises ST-RCGP scores under unchanged reported settings: October RMSE/NLPD changes from 0.73/1.42 to 0.50/0.63, while November changes from 0.79/1.33 to 1.19/2.44. Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. New well-log, sensitivity, timing, and coverage findings substantially expand the reported results.

T1.justification: New Proposition 3.2 and Appendix B.2 prove sequential/batch equivalence under identical priors, non-adaptive weights, and a Gauss-Markov assumption. The previous robustness theorem and proof are retained under new numbers. A new main-text score formula divides by sigma, inconsistently with the unchanged sigma-squared derivation in Appendix B.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: robust conjugate inference at STGP computational cost, improved handling of RCGP's three limitations, and competitive performance against robust alternatives. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies the distinction between fixed-weight equivalence and adaptive inference, attributes pre-outlier temperature differences to smoothing, and adds the limitation that sequential computation may be suboptimal when parallel hardware is available. Existing spatial-scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: New sensitivity analyses document the tested IMQ exponents and which parameters are held fixed or varied. Existing hardware, experiment hyperparameters, and code/data access statements are retained. The added well-log experiment supplies little fitting detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against outlier-rejection STGP work by Bock et al. and Waxman and Djurić, and more explicitly distinguishes earlier generalised-Bayes filters. Additional references support IMQ weighting, the equivalence proof, well-log data, and parallel smoothing.

P1.justification: Local rewrites expand the filtering and weight-function explanations, bring metric formulas into Section 4, and improve wording. An impact statement and appendix subsections are added, but the main narrative and much existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML-style document with a two-column main text, revised headers, and extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 12–17 add well-log fits, multi-panel sensitivity tests, timing comparisons, financial fits, and coverage plots.

improvement.justification: The controlled weight analyses and temperature-coverage checks provide useful evidence missing in v1, while the conditional equivalence proof improves theoretical clarity. Gains are limited: the retained robustness argument still invokes equivalence for adaptive weights, the new score formula introduces a scaling inconsistency, and Table 3 revisions are unexplained. Overall, support and clarity improve without resolving the main theoretical gap.
